Subject: One-off pricing matrix override — Zenith Health (VP signoff requested)

Team,

I wanted to surface a request from Zenith Health that needs VP/CFO level clearance before we can proceed. They are asking for a one-off adjustment to the pricing matrix for a 12-month committed pilot: a blended effective discount of ~37% on our published entry tier in exchange for a reference case and a three-month onboarding support credit.

Key quick facts (attached workbook):
- Expected first 6 months consumption: ~4.2M tokens/month (embedding-heavy pipeline).
- Upside scenario (post-pilot): potential multi-year expansion to our Dedicated offering; sales sees a >40% expansion probability if the pilot meets latency/cost targets.
- Requested concession: temporary reprice to the mid-tier metric with a further seat discount and waived onboarding fees.

Why this is different: Zenith requests an explicit override of our matrix (not a volume-based rebate) that would set a custom unit rate for the pilot period. That triggers our commercial guardrails. I recommended we document the expected unit economics and the downside protection mechanics.

I've attached: zenith_oneoff_impact_calculation.xlsx (breakdown), proposed_term_sheet_zenith.docx (redlines from sales), and a short exec memo (zenith_exec_memo_v1.pdf).

Ask: Kimberly/Jordan — can you review and provide the recommended approval path (VP vs CFO), and if approved, suggested guardrails (commit floors, true-up, makegood triggers)? Zenith needs a response by EOD PT today to keep their procurement window open.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0117
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: One-off pricing matrix override — Zenith Health (VP signoff requested)

Markus —

Reviewed the workbook. High level thoughts:

1) Economics: At the requested blended 37% discount our expected gross margin during the pilot drops below our support threshold unless we bind a minimum monthly consumption floor of 3M tokens and include a makegood if they underdeliver by >20%.
2) Risk control: Require a refundable onboarding deposit (applied to month 3) and explicit SLA steps for our escape (e.g., failure to meet latency SLA after two optimization cycles).
3) Approval level: This is material and nonstandard; recommend VP + CFO signoff. Jordan — please prepare an annotated term-sheet with these guardrails (I can draft the memo for CFO).

I will be available for a 30-min quick call at 10:30 PT if you want to go through the calculations before we send to the finance mailbox.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: One-off pricing matrix override — Zenith Health (VP signoff requested)

Thanks — attached is an annotated term sheet (proposed_term_sheet_zenith.docx) with the guardrails Kimberly suggested. Summary of changes I included:
- 3M token/mo minimum (true-up monthly)
- Onboarding deposit = 1 month at the agreed custom rate, refundable against month 3 usage
- Makegood clause: if usage < 80% of floor over first 60 days, pricing reverts and they are billed retroactively for the delta
- SLA escape: two remediation cycles then right to terminate pilot without penalty

Oliver — we incorporated your procurement team's timelines; can you confirm the reference case commitment if pilot passes and that they can commit to a public case study? That is a key part of the commercial rationale.

If Kimberly is good, I'll bundle this into an exec memo for CFO signoff.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Kimberly/Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround. Attaching the final exec memo for CFO review (zenith_exec_memo_v1.pdf) and the annotated term sheet.

CFO team — brief summary for your review: Zenith Health requests a one-off per-token reprice for a 12-month pilot that would meaningfully undercut our published entry tier. In exchange they will: serve as a named reference, provide a short technical deep-dive for our benchmark board, and commit to a procurement timeline that gets us to pilot in Q1. Our recommended controls: 3M token monthly floor, refundable onboarding deposit (1 month), makegood provision (re-bill if usage <80% of floor over first 60 days), and an SLA-based escape clause.

Requested action: VP + CFO signoff OR explicit escalation route by EOD PT. If approved, legal and sales will finalize and send a DocuSign link.
